title: What AML/CTF training do real estate agents need in Australia?
seoTitle: AML/CTF training for real estate agents
description: Which real estate businesses AUSTRAC regulates from July 1, 2026, who needs AML/CTF training before they start, and what evidence an agency should keep.
shortAnswer: Since July 1, 2026, Australian real estate businesses that broker the sale, purchase or transfer of real estate, or sell property without an independent agent, are reporting entities under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006. The Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre (AUSTRAC) expects every person in an AML/CTF related role to receive personnel due diligence and role appropriate training before they start, then refresher training while they stay in the role.
keyTakeaways: Two real estate designated services are regulated from July 1, 2026: brokering a sale, purchase or transfer (item 1 of table 5 in section 6) and selling real estate in a business without an independent agent (item 2), which captures developers selling off the plan.
A seller's agent treats both the seller and the buyer as customers, so agents need training on due diligence for the party they do not represent.

AUSTRAC's real estate starter kit requires personnel due diligence and role appropriate training before a person performs an AML/CTF related role, then ongoing due diligence, refresher training and performance monitoring.
AUSTRAC's Smart agent's guide to AML/CTF is a train the trainer package, but AUSTRAC says it does not fulfil an agency's obligation to provide training specific to its own business and risks.
Agents must recognize when to report: suspicious matters within 24 hours (terrorism financing) or 3 business days, and physical cash of $10,000 or more within 10 business days.
regulator: Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre (AUSTRAC)
appliesTo: Real estate agencies acting as seller's agents or buyer's agents
Property developers and other businesses selling house and land packages, apartments off the plan or subdivided land without an independent agent
Principals, agency leaders and the AML/CTF compliance officer
Sales agents, administrative staff and contractors who onboard customers or handle settlement communications

sections.heading: Which real estate businesses are regulated from July 1, 2026?

blocks.text: A real estate business is regulated if it provides one of two designated services with a geographical link to Australia: brokering the sale, purchase or transfer of real estate on behalf of a party, or selling or transferring real estate in the course of a business selling real estate where no independent agent brokers the sale. Both appear in table 5 of section 6 of the Act, as amended by the [Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Amendment Act 2024](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2024A00110/asmade/text).

AUSTRAC's [real estate designated services guidance](https://www.austrac.gov.au/new-austrac/designated-services-newly-regulated-entities/real-estate-designated-services) says the brokering service is typically provided by seller's and buyer's agents, and that the second service captures property developers and other businesses selling house and land packages, apartments off the plan and blocks of vacant land in new subdivisions, including where they use in house sales staff rather than an external agency. Incidental sales by a business and private sales of residential property are not captured.

The definition of real estate is wider than freehold. It covers fee simple interests, leasehold interests of more than 30 years (excluding renewal options), and land use entitlements conferred through shares in a company or units in a unit trust. AUSTRAC gives 99 year leases in the Australian Capital Territory, crown and pastoral leases, and residential site agreements longer than 30 years as examples. A transfer with no consideration, such as a family transfer, is still within scope.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the Act, the AML/CTF Rules 2025 and AUSTRAC guidance as at November 2026. AUSTRAC's real estate starter kit page was last updated on April 2, 2026 and the Smart agent's guide on July 31, 2026. Check the primary sources before relying on a date or threshold.

sections.heading: Who is the customer, and why does that change agent training?

blocks.text: For the brokering service, both the seller and the buyer are customers of the same agency, so an agent acting only for the vendor still has AML/CTF obligations toward the purchaser. This is the single biggest practical shift for sales staff, and training has to cover it explicitly.

Timing differs by role. AUSTRAC says a seller's agent starts providing the designated service to the seller when the agreement to broker the sale is signed, and to the buyer when it is reasonably expected that the transaction will proceed, typically when the offer is accepted and the contract is signed. A buyer's agent starts with the buyer when the agreement to find a property is signed, and with the seller at the same contract stage. For auctions, AUSTRAC notes that initial customer due diligence (CDD) may be delayed where completing it would disrupt the ordinary course of business, because the buyer may only be known after the fall of the hammer.

items: **Listing agents** need to know which checks are due at the agency agreement and which fall due at contract for the buyer.
**Auctioneers and sales support staff** need the delayed verification criteria and the steps to finish CDD after the auction.
**Developer sales teams** start the obligation at the commitment to sell, typically the agreement to sell, and the customer is the buyer or transferee.

sections.heading: What training must an agency provide, and when?

blocks.text: An agency must assess and train every person who performs an AML/CTF related role before they start that role and keep training them while they remain in it. The legal basis is section 26F(4)(d) and (e) of the Act and sections 5-8 and 5-9 of the AML/CTF Rules 2025, which the general [AUSTRAC AML/CTF training requirements](/regulations/austrac-aml-ctf-training-requirements) page explains in detail. This page covers how those obligations land in an agency.

AUSTRAC's [real estate program starter kit, step 2](https://www.austrac.gov.au/industry-and-business/obligations-and-guidance/program-starter-kits/real-estate-program-starter-kit/step-2-use-your-real-estate-program) sets out the sequence. Before a person performs an AML/CTF related role, the agency conducts initial personnel due diligence, confirms the person is suitable and eligible, and provides role appropriate AML/CTF training. While the person stays in the role, the agency conducts ongoing personnel due diligence, provides refresher or updated training as required, and monitors performance against AML/CTF responsibilities. When a person changes role or leaves, records, appointments and role based access are updated.

AUSTRAC's guidance on [identifying roles that need due diligence and training](https://www.austrac.gov.au/industry-and-business/obligations-and-guidance/your-amlctf-program/personnel-due-diligence-and-training/identifying-personnel-roles-require-due-diligence-and-training) extends the obligation beyond employees to contractors, consultants, paid and unpaid interns, and people employed by service providers the business uses. For agencies that rely on independent contractor sales agents, those agents are in scope.

sections.heading: What must real estate staff be able to recognize and report?

blocks.text: Frontline staff must be able to spot the real estate red flags AUSTRAC publishes and know the reporting timelines the agency is held to. AUSTRAC's [real estate risk insights](https://www.austrac.gov.au/industry-and-business/education-and-resources/publications-and-resources/risk-insights-and-indicators-suspicious-activity-real-estate-sector) say its money laundering national risk assessment found the real estate sector poses a high money laundering risk in Australia, and that real estate professionals are often the first contact point for criminals trying to launder money.

Indicators AUSTRAC lists for customers include avoiding face to face meetings, appearing to follow the instructions of third parties, seeming to know both sides of a sale, buying in the name of a third party, relative or minor with no legal or economic reason, offering higher commissions, and asking for a sudden change of ownership close to settlement. It also says foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) must always be treated as high risk customers.

blocks.text: Tipping off is the conversational risk most specific to sales roles. AUSTRAC's training package devotes its third module to client conversations, managing objections, avoiding tipping off and escalation, because agents often keep talking to a customer after a concern is raised internally.

sections.heading: How should an agency map roles to training and evidence?

blocks.text: An agency should list every role that touches an AML/CTF obligation, then set the training content, timing and audit evidence for each. The table below is an original, illustrative matrix for a residential agency built from the starter kit sequence and AUSTRAC's sector guidance. Frequencies are the agency's own policy choices, since the Rules set no fixed interval; the guide on [building a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) explains how to justify them.

blocks.text: For each record, capture the content version delivered so that, when the program changes, the agency can show who was trained on the superseded version and who has been retrained. The guide to [preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) covers register structure.

sections.heading: Can an agency rely on AUSTRAC's own training package?

blocks.text: An agency can use AUSTRAC's free materials as part of its training but cannot rely on them alone. AUSTRAC's [Smart agent's guide to AML/CTF](https://www.austrac.gov.au/industry-and-business/education-and-resources/smart-real-estate-agents-guide-amlctf) is a train the trainer package for frontline staff, including residential and commercial agents, buyer's agents and sales agents. AUSTRAC states that it "doesn't fulfil your business's obligation to provide training specific to your business and its ML/TF risks".

The package has three modules intended to be delivered in sequence: why AML/CTF matters, what to look for and what to do, and AML/CTF in practice. It includes an instructor guide and facilitation manual, role plays and pre and post training questionnaires, and AUSTRAC also publishes self paced videos covering the same learning outcomes. A sensible design is to use the package as the generic foundation, then add agency specific modules on the agency's own risk assessment, forms, escalation contacts and systems.

AUSTRAC's [good and poor practice examples](https://www.austrac.gov.au/industry-and-business/obligations-and-guidance/your-amlctf-program/personnel-due-diligence-and-training/examples-personnel-due-diligence-and-training-practice) include a fictional 25 person agency whose online vendor training did not cover real estate risks or refer to the agency's program, did not track completion or schedule refreshers, and did not confirm understanding. AUSTRAC presents that as a failure to meet the training obligation, which is a useful checklist of what to avoid when buying [off the shelf training](/compare/off-the-shelf-vs-custom-compliance-training).

sections.heading: What deadlines sit alongside the training obligation?

blocks.text: Training sits alongside enrollment and the appointment of an AML/CTF compliance officer, both of which have fixed deadlines. AUSTRAC's [enrollment guidance](https://www.austrac.gov.au/new-austrac/enrol-us/enrol-us-overview) says a business must apply to enrol no later than 28 days after it starts providing a designated service, and must update enrollment details within 14 days of a change.

AUSTRAC's [compliance officer guidance](https://www.austrac.gov.au/industry-and-business/obligations-and-guidance/your-amlctf-program/develop-your-amlctf-programs/step-1-establish-your-governance-framework/amlctf-compliance-officer) requires the officer to be appointed within 28 days of providing designated services, to be at management level, to be an Australian resident where services are provided through a permanent establishment in Australia, and to be a fit and proper person. Newly regulated entities had to notify AUSTRAC of their officer by the later of July 29, 2026 or 14 days after enrolling. In a small agency the officer is often the principal, who then needs the deepest training in the business.

AUSTRAC's real estate starter kit is designed for agencies with 15 or fewer personnel that do not offer fully remote self service. Larger or more complex agencies must assess whether the kit fits and will generally need stronger controls, which includes more differentiated role training.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps the real estate designated services, the customer timing rules and the agency's own risk assessment into a framework before any module is written, then links each role to the decisions it must make and the assessment that proves it can. When AUSTRAC updates its guidance or the agency changes its policies, the affected roles and assessments are identified from that framework.

faqs.q: Does a property manager need AML/CTF training?
faqs.a: The real estate designated services cover brokering a sale, purchase or transfer of real estate and selling real estate without an independent agent. Whether a property management role is in scope depends on whether that person performs functions relevant to the agency's AML/CTF obligations. Agencies that provide a regulated service should assess each role against their program rather than exempting a team by title.

faqs.q: Do independent contractor agents count as personnel?
faqs.a: Yes. AUSTRAC says personnel due diligence and training apply to people the business employs and to people it otherwise engages, such as contractors, consultants, interns and people employed by service providers it uses. Contractor sales agents who deal with customers need the same pre start training as employees.

faqs.q: Is annual AML/CTF training mandatory for real estate agents?
faqs.a: The Rules require initial training and ongoing training appropriate to the person's function, risks and responsibilities, but set no fixed interval. AUSTRAC's examples for customer facing roles use 12 months, and its good practice example uses at least annually or on significant change, so an annual cycle is a common, defensible choice.

faqs.q: Are property developers caught even if they use their own sales staff?
faqs.a: Yes. AUSTRAC says the second real estate designated service includes developers and other businesses selling house and land packages, apartments off the plan and new subdivision lots with in house agents or sales and marketing employees rather than an external agency.
